title: Rule sets, selectors, declarations, properties, values
learningObjectives: Explain and apply rule sets, selectors, declarations, properties, values.

understand.concept: A rule set contains a selector and declaration block. Each declaration pairs a property with a value, such as color: blue. Selectors determine which elements match.
understand.whyItMatters: HTML works without CSS, but CSS makes content clearer, more usable and adaptable to different screens.
understand.analogy: If HTML is a building's structure, CSS is its visual finish and interior design.
understand.analogyLimit: CSS is more than colour; it affects layout, responsive behaviour, interaction states and accessibility preferences.

explain.narrative: A rule set contains a selector and declaration block. Each declaration pairs a property with a value, such as color: blue. Selectors determine which elements match.

examples.code: Selectors and declarations
examples.explanation: Change the style rule and observe how colour, spacing and layout change.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser displays the HTML content according to the CSS declarations.

practise.guidedTask: Change one CSS property value and observe the result.
practise.independentTask: Design a small information card using semantic HTML and a reusable CSS rule.
hints: Identify which elements the selector matches.
Change one property at a time.

questions.prompt: In color: purple, what is purple?
questions.explanation: Keep the roles of HTML structure and CSS presentation distinct.

questions.prompt: Does using CSS remove the need for semantic HTML?
questions.explanation: HTML provides meaning and structure; CSS controls presentation.
